# landscape_LB_higgs_displaced

**AIDA-Scout S1b (landscape scalar cascades), benchmark `L-B-displaced`** -- generated by
`landscape/make_processes.py`.

The same h -> phi_i phi_j topology as `landscape_LB_higgs`, at the shipped lambda = 1e-4 rather than the retuned 2.7e-3.

**The pair is a controlled comparison, and it is unusually clean.** Measured side by side at 2000 events, the two points agree on parton multiplicity (12.39 vs 12.38), flavour composition, charged multiplicity (113 vs 113), HT (119 vs 121 GeV), leading jet pT (65 vs 67 GeV) and every L1 rate. The only thing that differs is **displacement**: the hidden scalars decay at a median r_xy of 2.6 mm here against 0.00 mm there, and 99.4% of signal charged particles come from beyond 100 um against 17.8%.

That makes this the point to use for any question of the form 'does displacement change what the trigger or the anomaly detector sees', with L-B as the null.

Reference: R. T. D'Agnolo, M. Ettengruber, L.-T. Wang, *Landscapes at
Colliders*, arXiv:2512.18001. The model is a Python port of the authors' Julia
code; see [`landscape/README.md`](../../landscape/README.md) for the port, its
eight-tier verification, and the deliberate deviations.

## Parameters

| | |
|---|---|
| N (number of singlet scalars) | 200 |
| lambda | 0.0001 |
| lambda' | 0.0001 |
| lambda'/lambda | 1 |
| M* | 10000 GeV |
| v2 | 221.4 GeV |
| mixing angle theta | 0.001 |
| mass spectrum | uniform on [0.7071, 10] GeV |
| **spectrum seed** | **424242** (one landscape realisation, fixed across jobs) |
| production | gg -> h -> phi_i phi_j |

## Normalisation

| | |
|---|---|
| cross section x BR | **0.003703 pb** |
| BR(h -> BSM), physical (Gamma_SM = 4.1e-3 GeV) | 0.0001514 |
| BR(h -> BSM), Julia normalisation (Gamma_bb(pole) x 1.89) | 7.633e-05 |
| Higgs signal-strength bound | 0.1 -- **within** |

lambda is the **shipped** 1e-4, not the retuned 0.0027 that `L-B` uses.
The rate is 730x lower, but that is not why this point exists: below the
hidden-pair threshold a scalar has no hidden channel open, so its width is pure
mixing and ctau goes as lambda^-2. At the shipped lambda those scalars live
730x longer, and the sample is **displaced** where L-B is prompt. It is a
different signature, not a weaker L-B.


## Lifetimes

```
Lifetimes: L-B-displaced
  200 scalars, hidden-pair threshold 2*m_min = 1.549 GeV
  ctau over the whole spectrum: min 1.708e-11  median 4.865e-11  max 4.233e+00 mm
  above threshold (182 scalars, hidden pair channel open): median 4.203e-11 mm  max 1.488e-07 mm
  below threshold (18 scalars = 9.0%, mixing only): median 2.725e+00 mm  max 4.233e+00 mm  <-- DISPLACED
```

Every cascade *terminates* on a sub-threshold scalar, so this displacement is
not a tail -- it is where essentially all the visible partons come from.


## Why it evades (or does not evade) the Phase-2 L1 menu

| Seed | Threshold | Fires? |
|---|---|---|
| PuppiHT | 450 (constituents pT > 30) | no -- 2.90% |
| SinglePuppiJet | 230 | no -- 2.35% |
| QuadJet | 400,70,55,40,40 | no -- the 400 GeV HT leg already fails |
| DoubleTkMuon (BPH) | 2,2, abs(eta)<1.5, dR<1.4, OS, dz<1cm | ~16% on paper -- **but see the d0 caveat** |
| DoubleTkMuon (central) | 4,4 | ~20% on paper -- **but see the d0 caveat** |
| DoubleTkElectron | 25,12 | no -- no electrons in the cascade |
| DoubleTkIsoPhoton | 22,12 | no -- the photon channel is below 0.1% |
| DoublePuppiTau | 52,52 | no |
| PuppiETmiss | 200 | no -- nothing escapes but tau neutrinos |


## What is in the LHE

The hidden scalars are written into the record, not just the final partons.
They share one PDG id (9000006) and each carries its own mass and its own
`VTIMUP`, because an LHE has nowhere else to put a per-particle displacement
and the cascade's decay vertices are the physics.

`LesHouches:setLifetime = 1` in the card is load-bearing: it is Pythia's
default, but `= 2` silently discards `VTIMUP` and collapses every hidden-scalar
decay vertex to the origin, making the sample prompt with no error. Verified by
A/B: with `= 1` the scalar decay vertices reach 232 mm; with `= 2` they are all
exactly zero.

Colour is connected **locally**: each phi -> q qbar is its own singlet with one
fresh tag, each phi -> g g its own closed loop with two. Connecting colour
across the cascade would string the whole event together and materially change
the hadronic activity.

## Measured, truth level, 2000 events, no pileup

Side by side with `landscape_LB_higgs` (the retuned, prompt point):

| | L-B (prompt) | this point (displaced) |
|---|---|---|
| parton multiplicity, mean | 12.38 | 12.39 |
| parton energy, median | 12.4 GeV | 12.3 GeV |
| charged multiplicity, median | 113 | 113 |
| jets above 30 GeV, median | 2 | 2 |
| HT, median | 121 GeV | 119 GeV |
| leading jet pT, median | 67 GeV | 65 GeV |
| HT > 450 | 2.70% | 2.90% |
| any jet > 230 | 2.15% | 2.35% |
| **hidden-scalar decay r_xy, median / 90% / max** | **0.00 / 0.08 / 0.40 mm** | **2.6 / 60 / 266 mm** |
| **signal charged displaced > 0.1 mm** | **17.8%** | **99.4%** |
| cross section x BR | 2.70 pb | 3.70e-3 pb |

Everything except the last two rows is the same point. That is the whole
argument for keeping both.

## The displacement survives PU 200 and Delphes

30 events each through the full chain, comparing `L1T_PUPPIPart_D0`:

| L1T PUPPI charged candidates | L-B (prompt) | this point |
|---|---|---|
| per event, pT > 2 GeV | 48.0 | 47.3 |
| of those, \|d0\| > 1 mm | 0.30 (0.6%) | **1.47 (3.1%)** |
| per event, pT > 5 GeV | 7.6 | 7.5 |
| of those, \|d0\| > 1 mm | 0.17 (2.2%) | **0.83 (11.2%)** |

A 5x enhancement in displaced L1 tracks that survives 200 pileup vertices.
Note the dilution: 99.4% of the *signal's* charged particles are displaced at
truth level, but the signal contributes a handful of candidates against ~1000
from pileup, so the whole-event displaced fraction is 3%, not 99%. Displacement
is a per-track handle here, not a per-event one.

This is also the check that `LesHouches:setLifetime = 1` is doing its job: the
proper decay lengths written into VTIMUP come out the other end as impact
parameters.

## Downstream limits

* `cards/delphes_card.dat` has **no d0 dependence** in its L1T tracking
  efficiencies -- they are functions of pt and eta only. The sample is correct
  at truth level, but the chain will not reproduce the loss of displaced tracks
  at L1. This matters most for `landscape_LB_higgs_displaced` and
  `landscape_LA_direct`.
* Delphes drops particles produced outside the tracker (R = 1.29 m, half-length
  3 m).
* **L1 menu decision bits are not produced here.** No CMSSW Phase-2 emulator
  exists in this repository; the menu column above is truth-level Pythia against
  the offline thresholds, which is an upper bound on what the real menu sees.

## Running

```bash
apptainer exec --bind $simdir \
  /cvmfs/unpacked.cern.ch/registry.hub.docker.com/jmduarte/mapyde:latest \
  sh $simdir/run.sh landscape_LB_higgs_displaced <nevents> <seed> $simdir False
```

This point uses the **pythia** branch of `run.sh`, with the landscape LHE
pre-step in front of it. `run.sh` runs `landscape.make_lhe` with the arguments
in `landscape_LB_higgs_displaced_lhe_args.dat`, writes the parton-level summary to
`outdir/parton_level.txt`, and then hands the LHE to the same Pythia -> HepMC
-> PU 200 -> Delphes -> parquet chain every other point uses.

To produce the LHE on its own, outside the job:

```bash
python3 -m landscape.make_lhe --benchmark L-B-displaced --fast-branching \
    --nevents 10000 --seed 1234 --out L-B-displaced.lhe --fragment L-B-displaced.cmnd
```
